subject: English
summaryPoints: Concession and contrast markers exhibit distinct syntactic behaviors: 'although' and 'even though' govern subordinate clauses (subject + verb), while 'in spite of' and 'despite' must be followed by a noun, gerund (-ing), pronoun, or the noun phrase 'the fact that'.
'Even though' serves as a more emphatic connector of contrast than 'although', whereas 'though' is versatile and can appear clause-initially, medially, or clause-finally (common in spoken English).

Sentence fragments are incomplete sentence structures lacking a grammatical subject, a finite predicate verb, or a complete thought, often formed when dependent clauses are mistakenly punctuated as independent sentences.

Pronunciation of the inflectional affix '-s/-es' follows voicing and sibilant rules: pronounced as /-iz/ after sibilants (/s/, /z/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/, /dʒ/), as /-s/ after voiceless consonants (/p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, /θ/), and as /-z/ after voiced sounds (/b/, /d/, /g/, /v/, /m/, /n/, /l/, /r/, vowels).

Pronunciation of regular past tense morpheme '-(e)d' depends on the final root phoneme: /-t/ after voiceless sounds (/p/, /k/, /f/, /s/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/), /-d/ after voiced sounds (/b/, /g/, /v/, /z/, /m/, /n/, /l/, vowels), and /-id/ after alveolar stops /t/ and /d/.
Sustainable development discourse requires balancing three interdependent pillars: economic development, environmental protection, and social equity.

formulas.label: Contrast: Clause vs Noun Phrase Formulas
formulas.expr: Although / Even though + Subject + Verb + , + Main Clause  |  Despite / In spite of + Noun Phrase / Gerund (V-ing) + , + Main Clause

formulas.label: Prepositional Concession with 'The Fact That'
formulas.expr: In spite of the fact that / Despite the fact that + Subject + Verb + , + Main Clause

formulas.label: Sentence Fragment Correction Rule
formulas.expr: Fragment: Subordinating Conjunction + S + V.  ->  Correct: Subordinating Conjunction + S + V + , + Independent Clause.

formulas.label: Past Morpheme '-(e)d' Allomorph Rule
formulas.expr: /t/ after voiceless (/p, k, f, s, ʃ, tʃ/)  |  /d/ after voiced (/b, g, v, z, m, n, l, vowels/)  |  /id/ after alveolar plosives (/t, d/)

examTip: A standard EUEE trap is placing a full clause directly after 'despite' or 'in spite of' without 'the fact that' (e.g., 'Despite he worked hard...' is incorrect; it must be 'Despite working hard...' or 'Although he worked hard...'). Also watch for 'although' used at the end of a sentence—only 'though' can appear sentence-finally.

keyDefinitions.definition: A group of words punctuated as a sentence that fails to express a complete thought because it lacks an independent subject, a finite verb, or both.
A cohesive discourse connective (such as although, even though, despite) used to link contrasting ideas where one fact renders another surprising.
A comprehensive development framework that meets present human needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs, balancing economic, social, and environmental pillars.
Any of two or more phonetic variants of a particular morpheme that occur in complementary distribution (e.g., /-s/, /-z/, /-iz/ for the plural affix or /-t/, /-d/, /-id/ for regular past tense).

eueeFocusTopics: Syntactic contrast between 'although/even though' (+ clause) and 'despite/in spite of' (+ noun phrase/gerund)
Identification and repair of sentence fragments (missing subject, verb, or complete thought)
Phonological pronunciation rules of past tense '-(e)d' (/-t/, /-d/, /-id/) and affix '-s' (/-s/, /-z/, /-iz/)
Reading comprehension and contextual vocabulary related to environmental conservation and SDGs
